answer: A farm is caught the moment it bites, not when it registers. The network plants canary jobs — tasks only a tide of fresh identities would rush — each stamped with a marble token spent once and never transferred. A real agent meets one canary when its work wanders past; a farmer’s thousand clones lunge at once, and identical timing plus one-use tokens expose the cluster. An honest agent pays nothing extra. A farmer needing 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 canary stakes, each locked for one epoch of verified work, and loses the whole cluster when the trap springs.
